stem: A producer tells a policyholder that her whole life policy's cash value will be forfeited next year unless she surrenders it now. The statement is false, and the producer is not offering her another policy. Under New Jersey law, this is:
options: Misrepresentation
Twisting
Churning
False advertising

stem: An agency's newspaper ad claims it has "won the state's top customer service award five years running." No such award exists. Which unfair trade practice is this?
options: False information and advertising
Defamation
Misrepresentation of policy terms
Twisting

stem: A producer tells prospects that a competing insurer "is about to be taken over by regulators," which is untrue, to steer new business away from that insurer. Which practice is this?
options: Defamation
Twisting
Rebating
Boycott

stem: Several insurers jointly threaten to stop writing business through any agency that also represents a new competitor, in order to keep that competitor out of the market. This is an example of:
options: Rebating
Unfair discrimination
Defamation
Boycott, coercion and intimidation

stem: Two applicants have the same age, health and risk class, with equal life expectancy. The underwriter charges one of them a higher life insurance rate because of the neighborhood he lives in. Under New Jersey law, this is:
options: Unfair discrimination
Permitted underwriting judgment
Rebating
A permitted territorial rating

stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the characteristics listed in New Jersey's ban on discrimination in issuing, withholding, extending or renewing a policy?
options: Creed
Ancestry
Occupation
National origin

stem: Which of the following is NOT treated as a rebate or unfair discrimination under New Jersey law?
options: Fair bonuses out of surplus paid only to friends
Premium abatements given as an inducement to buy
Modest stock gifts offered as an inducement to buy
Fair bonuses paid out of nonparticipating surplus
key: Fair bonuses paid out of nonparticipating surplus

stem: Which of the following, if an insurer does it routinely, is an unfair claim settlement practice in New Jersey?
options: Denying claims before reasonably investigating them
Refusing to pay claims for losses the policy excludes
Requiring a death certificate before paying a death claim
Paying claims only after a reasonable investigation
key: Denying claims before reasonably investigating them

stem: Membership in the New Jersey Life and Health Insurance Guaranty Association is:
options: Voluntary for insurers with strong financial ratings
A condition of an insurer's authority to do business in New Jersey
Required only of insurers that sell annuities
Required only of mutual insurers
key: A condition of an insurer's authority to do business in New Jersey

stem: After an insurer stops holding its New Jersey certificate of authority, it remains a member of the life and health guaranty association for:
options: 1 year
2 years
4 years
10 years

stem: For administration and assessment, the New Jersey Life and Health Insurance Guaranty Association maintains which two accounts?
options: A resident account and a nonresident account
An individual account and a group account
A life insurance and annuity account, and a health account
A premium account and a claims account
key: A life insurance and annuity account, and a health account

stem: An insured's life insurer becomes insolvent. Regardless of how many policies are involved, the guaranty association's limit for life insurance death benefits on one life is:
When a life insurer fails, the guaranty association's limit on a life policy's net cash surrender and withdrawal values, for one life, is:
For annuities, the guaranty association's limit on net cash surrender and withdrawal values for one life is:

Maria has a $400,000 life policy and an annuity with a $300,000 present value, both with the same insurer, which becomes insolvent. What is the most the guaranty association can be obligated to pay in total on these benefits for her?
The guaranty association's benefit limit for any one unallocated annuity contract is:
Under New Jersey's Life and Health Insurance Guaranty Association Act, the limit on benefits for an accident or health insurance policy is:
options: Unlimited

stem: A producer tells a hesitant client, "Don't worry about this insurer's finances, because the state guaranty association will cover you anyway." Under New Jersey law, this statement is:
options: Acceptable, because the association does exist
Required disclosure at the point of sale
Acceptable if the coverage limits are also stated
Prohibited use of the association to induce a purchase
key: Prohibited use of the association to induce a purchase

stem: When must a member insurer give the policyowner the guaranty association's summary document?
options: No later than the day the policy is handed over
Within 30 days after the policy is delivered
Only if the policyowner requests it in writing
Only after the insurer becomes impaired
key: No later than the day the policy is handed over

stem: The disclaimer on the guaranty association's summary document must warn that any available coverage is conditioned on:
options: Payment of an annual guaranty fee
Continued residence in New Jersey
The policy being in force for two years
The insured's good health at the time of insolvency

stem: New Jersey's prohibition on misleading policy comparisons applies when the comparison is used to induce someone to do which of the following?
options: Increase the face amount of an existing policy
Change the payment mode of an existing policy
Keep or convert a current policy
Add a rider to an existing policy
key: Keep or convert a current policy

stem: A producer tells a prospect that a participating policy "has paid 8% dividends every year for 20 years." Similar policies actually paid between 3% and 5%. Under New Jersey law, the statement is:
options: Permitted, since dividends are not guaranteed
Permitted if an illustration is also provided
Twisting
Misrepresentation

stem: An insurer sells a 10-year term policy under the product name "Lifetime Wealth Builder." Under New Jersey law, this is:
options: Misrepresentation of what the product is
Permitted, because product names are marketing
Twisting
Permitted if the policy form says it is term insurance
key: Misrepresentation of what the product is

stem: A producer offers to give a new life insurance client half of the producer's commission on the policy. Under New Jersey law, this is:
options: Commission splitting, which is legal between licensed persons
An illegal rebate
Permitted, because the client is not licensed
A permitted marketing allowance

stem: Before the commissioner can order a person to stop an unfair life or annuity trade practice, what must the commissioner first serve on that person?
options: A cease and desist order effective immediately
A notice of a hearing only
A statement of charges and notice of a hearing
A civil complaint filed in Superior Court
key: A statement of charges and notice of a hearing
